claims.claim: (a) The TOML rule struct SubscriptionRule carries require_mention with a serde default attribute, so a hand-written rule that omits the key deserializes with mention OFF (bool default = false).
claims.notes: The struct is #[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)] (filter.rs:82); serde's #[serde(default)] on a bool yields false when the TOML key is absent. The explicit Default impl (filter.rs:122) also sets require_mention: false. Rules are parsed from [[rules]] tables in the file given by --config / BUZZ_ACP_CONFIG (default ./buzz-acp.toml, config.rs:336-337) via load_rules (config.rs:1161).

claims.claim: (b) Three subscribe modes exist: Mentions (default), All, Config. subscribe=config means per-channel NIP-01 filters are derived by merging the [[rules]] loaded from the TOML config file instead of a synthesized built-in rule.

citations.quote: pub enum SubscribeMode { Mentions, All, Config, }
Same merge logic as resolve_channel_filters() Config branch

claims.notes: resolve_channel_filters (config.rs:1234-1326) builds a ChannelFilter {kinds, require_mention} per channel. Config branch: kinds are unioned across matching rules (empty = wildcard, config.rs:1298-1306); channels with no matching rule are omitted entirely (config.rs:1312, and resolve_single_channel_filter returns None, config.rs:1403-1407). In config mode --kinds, --channels and --no-mention-filter are ignored with warnings (config.rs:889-899).

claims.claim: (c) Runtime consequence of require_mention=false in a config-mode rule: the merged ChannelFilter starts at require_mention=true but any matching rule with false flips it (most-permissive-wins); the relay REQ then omits the #p mention tag filter, so the relay delivers every channel event of the subscribed kinds; match_event then skips the mention check for that rule, so the agent is queued/prompted for every such event from any author allowed by the inbound author gate (default owner-only), not just @mentions.
claims.notes: Full hop chain: config.rs:1290 seeds require_mention=true; 1307-1309 flips to false for any rule that has the default; lib.rs:1533 sends the ChannelFilter to the relay task; relay.rs:3194-3196 only inserts "#p":[agent_pubkey] into the NIP-01 REQ when require_mention is true ("#h" channel tag is always present, relay.rs:3191). With #p omitted the relay delivers all events in the channel matching kinds. Inbound events pass the author gate (lib.rs:2233-2242, mode default owner-only per README.md:138 and config.rs:448/1096), then match_event: the mention check (filter.rs:390-399) only runs when rule.require_mention is true, so a default rule matches without any p-tag. Matched events are queue.push'd (lib.rs:2269) and drained into batched ACP prompts. Net effect: a hand-written [[rules]] entry omitting require_mention makes the agent react to EVERY message of the rule's kinds in the channel from gate-allowed authors (all owner messages by default; everyone's with --respond-to anyone).

claims.claim: (d) NEGATIVE: the false default of require_mention and its subscription-widening consequence are not documented anywhere for rule authors — no README section, docs/ page, or user-facing doc describes the [[rules]] schema, subscribe=config usage, or the default value.

If `true`, the event must contain a `p` tag referencing the agent

search_method.false_positives: 3 inspected and discarded: (1) README.md:238-242 shows require_mention=false but inside a '[channel.CHANNEL_UUID]' example — a config shape load_rules does not parse (TomlConfig has only a 'rules' field, config.rs:1155-1159, no deny_unknown_fields, so [channel.*] tables are silently ignored) and it states no default; (2) README.md:249 documents mentions-mode behavior, not the config-mode rule default; (3) ARCHITECTURE.md:666 is a file-size table row ('filter.rs | 814 | Subscription rules, evalexpr filtering') — developer inventory, no schema or defaults. The rustdoc on the field (filter.rs:91-93) describes what true means but never states the default; #[serde(default)] is visible only to source readers, not rule authors.
search_method.falsifier: Any future commit that (1) adds a README/docs section documenting subscribe=config and the [[rules]] TOML schema stating that require_mention defaults to false, (2) makes a new .md file match 'require_mention', or (3) changes the serde default (e.g. #[serde(default = ...)] returning true) would falsify this claim.

claims.notes: The README documents only mentions/all modes ('--subscribe all', README.md:232-234) and an inbound-author-gate section; '--subscribe config' and the [[rules]] format the parser actually reads (verified by test TOML at config.rs:1957-1964 using [[rules]]) are documented nowhere.

claims.claim: (e) Mentions mode forces require_mention=true (both in the channel subscription filter and in the synthesized matching rule) unless the explicit --no-mention-filter escape hatch is set; All mode hardcodes it to false.
claims.notes: no_mention_filter is a clap bool flag, default false, so mentions mode yields require_mention=true by default (test config.rs:1510; the --no-mention-filter override tested at config.rs:1530-1538). The same logic applies in resolve_single_channel_filter for dynamically discovered channels (config.rs:1362-1371). In config mode --no-mention-filter is explicitly ignored with a warning (config.rs:896-898), so the only mention control there is the per-rule field with its undocumented false default. setup_mode's built-in rule also uses require_mention: true (setup_mode.rs:545-556).

extra_findings: 1) Documentation/parser mismatch: the only README TOML example containing require_mention uses a '[channel.CHANNEL_UUID]' table (crates/buzz-acp/README.md:238-242), but load_rules deserializes TomlConfig which has only a 'rules' field with no deny_unknown_fields (crates/buzz-acp/src/config.rs:1155-1159), so that documented shape is silently ignored — a user following the README gets zero rules and, in config mode, only the 'config file contains zero rules' warning (config.rs:1176-1181). 2) Asymmetric merge semantics amplify the surprise: with multiple rules on one channel, one lax rule (require_mention=false, i.e. the default) removes the #p filter from the shared channel subscription (config.rs:1307-1309, test 'most permissive (false) should win' at 1901-1914); strict rules still enforce mention per-rule inside match_event (filter.rs:390-399), but the relay now delivers all channel traffic to the harness. 3) Blast radius is bounded by the inbound author gate, default owner-only (README.md:138-148; lib.rs:2233-2242): with defaults the agent reacts to every owner message in the channel without any @mention; with --respond-to anyone it reacts to every user's messages of the rule's kinds. 4) FASE-2 wording nuance: the serde default is a property of the SubscriptionRule struct itself (mode-independent), but it only takes effect in subscribe=config since that is the only mode reading hand-written rules; in that mode --no-mention-filter is ignored (config.rs:896-898).
